generationContext.text:
# Azure Search performance tests

The assets in this area comprise a set of performance tests for the [Azure Search client library for .NET](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/tree/main/sdk/search/Azure.Search.Documents) and its associated ecosystem.  The artifacts in this library are intended to be used primarily with the Azure SDK engineering system's testing infrastructure, but may also be run as stand-alone applications from the command line.

## Contributing

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions.  Most contributions require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use your contribution. For details, visit https://cla.microsoft.com.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately (e.g., label, comment). Simply follow the instructions provided by the bot. You will only need to do this once across all repos using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/). For more information see the [Code of Conduct FAQ](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/) or contact [opencode@microsoft.com](mailto:opencode@microsoft.com) with any additional questions or comments.

Please see our [contributing guide](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information.

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <AssemblyTitle>Microsoft Azure.Search.Documents client library</AssemblyTitle>
    <Version>12.1.0-beta.3</Version>
    <!--The ApiCompatVersion is managed automatically and should not generally be modified manually.-->
    <ApiCompatVersion>12.0.0</ApiCompatVersion>
    <Description>
      This is the Azure AI Search client library for developing .NET
      applications with rich search experiences.  It enables you to query your
      indexes, update documents in your indexes, and manage indexes, synonym
      maps, indexers, data sources, or other service-level resources.
    </Description>
    <PackageTags>Azure AI Search;Azure Search Documents;Azure Search;Search;AI Search;Search Engine;Azure</PackageTags>
    <DisableEnhancedAnalysis>true</DisableEnhancedAnalysis>
    <TargetFrameworks>$(RequiredTargetFrameworks)</TargetFrameworks>
    <IncludeOperationsSharedSource>true</IncludeOperationsSharedSource>
    <AotCompatOptOut>true</AotCompatOptOut>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Pull in Shared Source from Azure.Core -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzureEventSource.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzureKeyCredentialPolicy.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)ExperimentalAttribute.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzureResourceProviderNamespaceAttribute.cs" LinkBase="Shared\Core" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)ForwardsClientCallsAttribute.cs" LinkBase="Shared\Core" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)PageResponseEnumerator.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)AzurePipelineResponse.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Azure.Core" />
    <PackageReference Include="System.ClientModel" />
    <PackageReference Include="System.Net.ServerSentEvents" />
    <PackageReference Include="System.Threading.Channels" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

proposals.explanation: CustomEntity explicitly declares get-only IList<CustomEntityAlias> Aliases. The adjacent comment identifies the intent to hide a generated public setter; generated output is not supplied, and collection immutability is not established.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated partial contains an explicit get-only declaration and a specific generated-setter customization comment, not merely a model name.

proposals.explanation: CustomEntityLookupSkill explicitly declares get-only IList<CustomEntity> InlineEntitiesDefinition, with a comment identifying generated-setter hiding as its intent. No generated comparison is supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated partial pairs a concrete accessor shape with an explicit statement of the generated API customization.

proposals.explanation: PendingQueueResized declares a Verbose EventSource event and writes its event identifier with sender type, endpoint and queue size.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A concrete non-Generated event method supplies custom payload and severity metadata plus a WriteEvent body; this is not an imported logger alone.

proposals.explanation: RetryQueueResized declares a Verbose event and writes the retry-queue event identifier, sender type, endpoint and queue size.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated event source implements this distinct queue-state event rather than merely referencing telemetry infrastructure.

proposals.explanation: BatchSubmitted declares an Informational event and writes its event identifier with sender type, endpoint and batch size; an invocation site for this event is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete custom event declaration and body occur outside Generated; runtime invocation is not inferred.

proposals.explanation: BatchActionCountUpdated declares a Warning event with sender type, endpoint, old count and new count. The batch-tuning algorithm invoking it is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A non-Generated EventSource method explicitly implements this payload and severity; it does not by itself prove active batch-size adjustment.

proposals.explanation: SearchIndexingBufferedSenderDisposedWithPendingActions declares an Error event writing sender type, endpoint and unsent-action count. No disposal call site for this event is supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The custom event method and payload are explicitly implemented outside Generated; the event's occurrence is not asserted.

proposals.explanation: PublishingDocuments declares a Verbose event writing sender type, endpoint and the flush flag. The supplied PublishAsync body calls this event before assembling batches.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete event implementation is in non-Generated source, with a concrete invocation in the supplied publisher implementation.

proposals.explanation: The string ActionNotificationEventHandlerExceptionThrown overload writes an Error event with sender, endpoint, action and exception text. Its NonEvent Exception overload converts e.ToString() and forwards to that event method.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both overload bodies and their Event/NonEvent distinction are supplied outside Generated; handler invocation and exception-catching behavior are not supplied.

proposals.explanation: BatchActionPayloadTooLarge declares a Warning event writing component type, endpoint and batch-action count. No payload-size limit or HTTP-status handling is established by this event method.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete event declaration/body are supplied outside Generated, but the triggering algorithm is excluded.

proposals.explanation: WriteInternal awaits ChannelWriter.WriteAsync in async mode; synchronous mode tries TryWrite and, if it fails, blocks on WriteAsync with the same cancellation token. It does not assume TryWrite cannot fail.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated batching helper explicitly implements both paths, and supplied publisher methods call it rather than a generated operation.

proposals.explanation: IndexActionCompletedEventArgs<T> exposes get-only Result. Its constructor delegates sender, action, execution mode and cancellation to the base class, asserts a nonnull result and assigns it.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated batching source provides a complete public event-payload constructor and extra state, not empty model scaffolding.

proposals.explanation: IndexActionEventArgs<T> exposes get-only Sender and Action, asserts both nonnull in its constructor, and passes execution mode and cancellation to SyncAsyncEventArgs.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-Generated public payload class supplies constructor validation/state and an explicit base initialization.

proposals.explanation: IndexActionFailedEventArgs<T> exposes Result and Exception. After delegating common arguments to the base constructor, its body assigns both without local null validation; no event-raising implementation is supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated payload implementation explicitly carries failure information, rather than merely documenting an event type.

proposals.explanation: Update increments the throttled-attempt counter on true, computes a left-shift retry multiplier times Random.Next over integer 80%-120% Delay bounds, applies Math.Min with MaxDelay, and records a wall-clock deadline. False resets the counter and deadline.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated retry helper implements the actual state update and delay expression; no policy dependency or HTTP-status name is used as substitute evidence.

proposals.explanation: SubmitBatchAsync awaits WaitIfNeededAsync before OnSubmitBatchAsync and feeds its returned throttled boolean into Update. WaitIfNeededAsync delays the remaining wall-clock interval when nonnegative, passing cancellation to Task.Delay; the actual submission implementation is abstract.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both the non-Generated delay body and its concrete placement around the abstract submission call are supplied.

proposals.explanation: ObjectNotDisposedException is an internal InvalidOperationException subclass whose constructor forwards its message to the base constructor. The supplied excerpt does not show a throw site or finalizer activation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated batching source declares a distinct exception type with a base initializer, not an empty partial declaration; the documentation's activation claim is not treated as runtime evidence.

proposals.explanation: Publisher<T> initializes an unbounded single-reader channel and asynchronous-continuation flush source, normalizes nonpositive flush intervals to null, selects fallback batch limits, configures supplied retry delays, and schedules ProcessMessagesAsync with the publisher cancellation token.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated internal publisher supplies explicit field initialization and startup code for its own batching runtime; no derived sender activation is inferred.

proposals.explanation: AddDocumentsAsync checks disposal and writes Message.Publish(documents) through the channel adapter using the caller's sync/async mode and cancellation token.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated publisher contains the actual producer method and channel write; the Message.Publish implementation is not supplied.

proposals.explanation: OnDocumentsAddedAsync enqueues keyed actions and logs pending count. With AutoFlush it publishes when combined pending/retry count is strictly greater than BatchActionCount, then starts a timer if work remains. HasBatch's explicit flush mode instead tests count greater than zero.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete non-Generated queueing, count projection and threshold code are supplied; the strict greater-than test is reported as written, not changed to a greater-than-or-equal threshold.

proposals.explanation: FlushInternal captures the current completion awaitable before enqueueing a flush message and then awaits or blocks according to mode. OnFlushedAsync calls PublishAsync with flush true, replaces the completion source, and resolves the previous source; FlushAsync is its disposal-guarded entry point.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both sides of the non-Generated flush protocol are supplied, including source rotation rather than an inferred successful flush guarantee.

proposals.explanation: ProcessMessagesAsync waits and reads using PublisherCancellationToken, sequentially awaits publish/flush handlers, throws for an unexpected message operation, and calls StopTimer after normal loop exit. No finally-based timer cleanup is shown.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated publisher implements the dispatch loop itself; its behavior is not inferred from the Channels dependency.

proposals.explanation: On the first successful disposed-flag exchange, DisposeAsync flushes, disposes the timer, completes the channel writer, waits for the reader in sync/async mode, and cancels the current flush source. The disposal interfaces choose that mode; exceptions can interrupt this ordered path.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-Generated lifecycle method and both interface adapters are supplied, rather than only IDisposable declarations.

proposals.explanation: EnsureNotDisposed throws ObjectDisposedException when _disposed is greater than zero, naming SearchIndexingBufferedSender<T> through nameof. The supplied AddDocumentsAsync and FlushAsync entry points call this guard.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated guard body and concrete callers are supplied; it is distinct from the separately declared ObjectNotDisposedException type.

proposals.explanation: PublishAsync stops the timer and uses a do/while submission loop, filling from retries before pending actions. Its local fill function respects BatchActionCount and stops at a repeated head key within that queue-fill call. The key set is recreated for each queue, not shared across retry and pending fills.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated method supplies the actual queue-selection, batch-building and submission-loop code; no byte limit or globally deduplicated batch is inferred.

proposals.explanation: The single-action EnqueueRetry compares the old RetryAttempts value with MaxRetries and postincrements it unless skipIncrement bypasses both operations. Its collection overload unconditionally enqueues supplied actions and logs retry count; the single-action overload uses it only when retriable.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both non-Generated overload bodies explicitly implement budget/queue behavior; no retryable HTTP-status policy is supplied.

proposals.explanation: StartTimer acts only with AutoFlush and an interval, casts total milliseconds to int and creates a one-shot timer or rearms a paused one, not an already-running timer. StopTimer pauses an existing active timer by assigning infinite due time and period.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated start/stop bodies explicitly implement timer-state handling. The excerpt cuts off inside OnTimerElapsed, so callback completion and exception behavior are not inferred.

decisions.reason: Lines 8-12 declare a get-only property and state an intent to hide a generated setter, but neither a generated counterpart nor a suppression/rename is supplied; the declaration alone does not establish the effective API change.
Lines 8-12 show a get-only partial-model property and a comment claiming setter hiding, but no generated counterpart or suppression is supplied to demonstrate the claimed change to the effective API.

The non-Generated method writes its declared queue-size EventSource event, and Publisher<T>.OnDocumentsAddedAsync and PublishAsync in the supplied fragment call it; the finding only describes the event implementation.
The method implements a distinct retry-queue diagnostic event; supplied Publisher<T>.PublishAsync and EnqueueRetry call it. Its event payload and severity are accurately cited.
The method declares and can write an event, but no call site for BatchSubmitted is supplied; an event declaration alone does not demonstrate that the SDK emits submitted-batch telemetry.

The Warning event implementation is present, but the supplied batching body neither changes BatchActionCount after construction nor calls BatchActionCountUpdated; active adjustment telemetry remains unmeasured.

The Error event method is defined, but the supplied Publisher<T>.DisposeAsync does not call it and the separate buffered-sender disposal implementation is absent; emission on disposal is not established.
Both the implemented EventSource method and its direct invocation before Publisher<T>.PublishAsync assembles batches are cited. The finding does not infer unrelated telemetry.

Both overload bodies are supplied, but no notification-handler invocation or error-catching call site is; converting an exception to text in a callable helper does not establish active SDK notification diagnostics.

The Warning event method exists, but no invocation or oversized-payload handling is supplied. The documented batch payload size is explicitly marked unused in Publisher<T>, so the event cannot establish active size tuning.

The complete non-Generated method implements asynchronous writing and a synchronous TryWrite/fallback path, and the publisher calls it; the cited behavior is not inferred from the Channels dependency.
The public payload class has its own Result accessor and constructor that validates and assigns it; this is substantive non-Generated model behavior, without asserting that an event was raised.
The public event-argument class declares Sender and Action and its constructor validates and assigns both while forwarding execution context to its base.
The distinct public failure payload declares Result and Exception and its constructor assigns both without local validation; the finding correctly avoids asserting that any event is raised.

Update implements the cited jittered capped backoff calculation and resets both the attempt count and deadline on a non-throttled result. It does not claim a particular HTTP status triggers this path.
The wait body and its placement before the abstract OnSubmitBatchAsync call, followed by throttle feedback to Update, are both supplied; no concrete HTTP submission outcome is inferred.

The internal exception type only forwards a constructor message; no supplied code constructs, throws or catches it. Its comment about finalizers cannot establish an activated error-handling customization.

The abstract publisher's constructor and field initializers implement channel, flush and retry setup and schedule its own processing loop; the finding does not assume an omitted concrete sender is instantiated.
The method guards disposal and forwards Message.Publish(documents) via the supplied channel adapter. It does not attribute behavior to the absent Message.Publish body.

The cited non-Generated methods implement pending enqueue, combined pending/retry count, a strict greater-than auto-flush threshold and a separate greater-than-zero flush test; they do not imply byte-size enforcement.

FlushInternal captures the current completion task before sending a flush message; OnFlushedAsync replaces the source and resolves the old one after PublishAsync returns. Both sides of this synchronization behavior are supplied.
The supplied loop serially reads and dispatches Publish/Flush operations and stops the timer only on normal loop exit; missing Message internals do not affect this bounded observation.
DisposeAsync implements the stated single-entry ordered sequence and both disposal interface adapters select its mode; the finding explicitly avoids guaranteeing completion on an exception.
The body throws ObjectDisposedException for a positive disposed flag and both cited entry points call it; this is not the separate unused ObjectNotDisposedException type.

PublishAsync contains a retry-first, count-limited batch-building loop; its local key set is freshly allocated per queue-fill call, so the finding correctly limits its duplicate-key claim and avoids assuming byte caps.
Both overloads implement retry budgeting and enqueueing; skipIncrement short-circuits the postincrement comparison. The proposal makes no unsupported claim about which HTTP errors are retryable.
StartTimer and StopTimer implement the cited guarded one-shot timer setup/rearming and pause behavior; the proposal correctly reserves the incomplete callback outcome.

omissions.explanation: OnTimerElapsed begins a synchronous channel write of Message.Flush and calls EnsureCompleted on that operation; its remaining callback and exception behavior are outside the excerpt.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The non-Generated Publisher<T> excerpt includes an actual timer callback body with a flush-message write, distinct from the proposed timer start/stop methods.

limitations: Ten evidence fragments span ten source paths, versus collector metadata of 1389 discovered, 1225 eligible and 10 captured files, with extensive named skips. Publisher.cs is restricted to lines 1-588 and ends inside a try block. This is partial discovery, not a whole-package customization count or absence assertion.

All collector kinds are unknown. The supplied .NET guideline's non-Generated layout is used with concrete internal runtime/helper implementations and the explicit setter-hiding comments. Generated counterparts, public sender wiring and concrete service submission implementations are not supplied.

Publisher<T> is an abstract internal batching component. GetDocumentKey, GetEndpoint and OnSubmitBatchAsync have no bodies here, and Message, PublisherAction and derived sender implementations were skipped. The reported algorithms do not establish successful service requests, actual throttle-status classification, partial-failure notification, batch-size tuning or public API activation.

The local fill function creates a fresh key set on every queue-fill call. It does not establish uniqueness across both retry and pending portions of one batch or drop duplicate documents. HasBatch uses a strict greater-than threshold, and PublishAsync enters a do/while body even before testing remaining-work eligibility.

BatchPayloadSize is explicitly marked not used yet in this excerpt; no byte-bounded submission is inferred. The referenced default batch constants are not supplied, and constructor retry delays override the helper's standalone defaults.

The retry calculation is the shown integer shift/jitter/Math.Min expression, not an independently proven safe monotonic exponential policy for arbitrary inputs or attempt counts. Waiting uses wall-clock DateTimeOffset.Now, and only abstract submission feedback determines the throttled boolean.

Event declarations are counted as implemented telemetry behavior, not proof that every event fires. Several invocation sites, the diagnostic exception's throw sites and finalizer behavior are absent. ObjectNotDisposedException and the actually thrown ObjectDisposedException guard are distinct types.

The timer is not rearmed while already running; this is not evidence of an inactivity debounce after every added document. OnTimerElapsed is truncated after its channel write, so no complete callback cleanup or exception policy is claimed.

The frozen target is module-v1, while the supplied package project and latestRelease both say 12.1.0-beta.3 and ApiCompatVersion says 12.0.0. No release-major identity migration is inferred. Performance-project metadata, standalone constants, empty scaffolding, abstract signatures and simple configuration properties are not separately inflated into findings.
Only the frozen request was used for SDK source. Findings are proposals pending independent review, not human-verified observations; human overrides remain authoritative.

The frozen target is dotnet:Azure.Search.Documents:module-v1. The supplied project file reports Version 12.1.0-beta.3 and ApiCompatVersion 12.0.0; neither changes the target's frozen module-major identity.

Coverage is partial: 10 captured fragments, not 10 complete distinct source files; Publisher.cs ends at line 588 inside OnTimerElapsed. Of 1,389 discovered files and 1,225 eligible files, 148 named paths or truncations were skipped. This review cannot assert package-wide absence or complete counts.

Evidence kind is unknown for every fragment. Non-Generated paths and substantive bodies support the accepted implementation findings, but no generated counterparts, emitter output or SDK execution were provided. The two get-only partial-model properties' claimed generated-setter suppression cannot be verified.

No supplied caller establishes activation of BatchSubmitted, BatchActionCountUpdated, SearchIndexingBufferedSenderDisposedWithPendingActions, ActionNotificationEventHandlerExceptionThrown or BatchActionPayloadTooLarge. Likewise no supplied finalizer uses ObjectNotDisposedException. These are unmeasured, not claims of package-wide nonuse.

The concrete OnSubmitBatchAsync implementation, derived publisher construction, event raising for the three public event-argument types, Message helpers and the rest of the timer callback are absent. No HTTP retryability, successful publication, finalizer behavior or complete disposal outcome is inferred.

The supplied code marks BatchPayloadSize unused and demonstrates count-based batching, not a byte-size limit. FillBatchFromQueue creates a new key set for each queue fill, not one set shared across retries and pending actions.

The proposed generatorAddressable=yes values indicate plausible generalizable code-generation shapes, not measured generator support, recurrence across services, reducibility or runtime activation. Acceptance is AI review only; human corrections and overrides remain authoritative.
